title: Localized thickness refinement on critical middle layers with ±2% bounds
scientific_hypothesis: The middle layers (4-6) of the chirped HfO2/SiO2 stack exhibit highest sensitivity in the transfer matrix formalism; constraining optimization to ±2% variance around Round 2 Candidate 2 thickness values for these layers while allowing broader variation on outer layers will capture remaining spectral broadening capacity without destabilizing the passband.
design_principle: Localized refinement preserves the verified interference mechanism from prior rounds while focusing search effort on the most thickness-sensitive regions. Outer layers maintain broader bounds to accommodate passband AR function, while middle layers use tight bounds to fine-tune stopband edge positions.
proposed_topology: 11-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | Fused silica. Exact layer sequence: HfO2(1), SiO2(2), HfO2(3), SiO2(4), HfO2(5), SiO2(6), HfO2(7), SiO2(8), HfO2(9), SiO2(10), HfO2(11).
design_variables: Layer thicknesses with differentiated bounds: layers 1-3 and 7-11: 20-120 nm; layers 4-6: seeded from Round 2 Candidate 2 (48.5, 78.8, 82.9 nm) with ±2% bounds (47.5-49.5, 77.2-80.4, 81.2-84.6 nm)
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and SiO2 are conventional evaporatable/sputterable dielectrics
Tight bounds on layers 4-6 require high deposition precision
theory_basis: Transfer matrix sensitivity analysis indicates middle layers in chirped stacks dominate stopband edge positioning
Prior iteration evidence shows 0.1243 score improvement possible with thickness optimization
expected_advantages: Focused search on high-sensitivity layers reduces optimization dimensionality
Preserves successful interference mechanism from Round 2
Tight bounds prevent destabilization of achieved passband performance
known_risks: ±2% bounds may be too restrictive if optimal solution lies outside this range
HfO2 absorption at deep UV wavelengths may limit maximum achievable transmittance
11-layer topology already tested in prior rounds; may have reached local optimum
execution_request_english: Optimize an 11-layer HfO2/SiO2 alternating stack on fused silica substrate under air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2. Thickness bounds: layers 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11: 20-120 nm; layer 4 (SiO2): 47.5-49.5 nm seeded at 48.5 nm; layer 5 (HfO2): 77.2-80.4 nm seeded at 78.8 nm; layer 6 (SiO2): 81.2-84.6 nm seeded at 82.9 nm. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with Round 2 Candidate 2 thicknesses as initial seed. Evaluate transmittance at normal incidence across 255-280 nm (maximize), 300-700 nm (minimize), and 700-1100 nm (minimize). No metal layers permitted. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 255–280 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Transmittance in 300–700 nm; Transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: Maximum 30 layers; No metal layers; Only conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Follows feedback directive to initiate localized refinement using Round 2 Candidate 2 as seed with ±2% variance on layers 4-6 identified as thickness-sensitive. Differentiated bounds focus optimization on critical middle layers while allowing outer layers to adjust for passband AR function.
